newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks slip in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks slip in thin trade.

text.p: Shares on the Amman stock exchange slipped in thin trade on Tuesday but some select activity led by Middle East Investment Bank cushioned the fall, dealers said.

The Amman Financial Market 60-share index shed 0.27 percent to 146.72 points from 147.11 points on Monday. Twenty two stock declined against only four advancing and 12 closed unchanged. A total of 374,753 shares changed hands for 443,709 dinars.

Brokers said the Jordanian stock exchange, highly sensitive to Middle East peace moves, was partly buoyed psychologically by King Hussein's first visit on Tuesday to the West Bank since he lost the territory to Israel in the Six-Day War in 1967.
"Some movement on three stocks helped to underpin the market, with the king's visit to the West Bank also buoying sentiment," one broker said.
The market has been dogged lately by an impasse in Palestinian-Israeli talks and growing doubts that neighbouring Iraq will be able to sell oil before the end of the year.
Brokers say the Central Bank's high interest rates policy has dampened investment by institutional investors, including banks, in the market.
Banks, who have shunned the market in favour of higher yield instruments, are waiting on the sidelines further adding to the woes of the cash-short exchange, dealer say.
Busiest shares for the second day in a row were Livestock and Poultry and Middle East Investment Bank along with Jordan Islamic Bank.

Brokers said long-term holders of Livestock and Poultry who saw their shares fall by a third in the last two weeks, were behind persistent speculative trade trying to prop it up. But the stock still fell 0.02 to 0.64 dinars after trade worth 141,000 dinars.

Rumoured foreign interest in Middle East Investment Bank's planned capitalisation issue to meet Central Bank guidelines by year-end appeared to motivate mostly floor traders interest in the bank stock, traders said.
MEIB shares rose 0.02 dinars to 1.14 dinars after trade worth 65,000 dinars.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.12 percent to 80.71 points from 80.81 points, 15.49 percent down from the same time last year.
A total of 223,978 shares worth 91,718 dinar changed hands in thin trade in the parallel market.
